How the calculation works

Midrank percentile = (Below + 0.5 × Equal) ÷ (Below + Equal + Above) × 100

A worked example

If 18 students score below you, three including you share your score, and nine score above, the class size is 30. Your midrank percentile is (18 + 1.5) ÷ 30 × 100 = 65.

Before you use the result

Counts refer to the same assessment and class group. Include yourself among tied students. This tool uses the midrank convention, not an official standardized-test percentile. Other conventions handle ties differently. A percentile rank is distinct from the percentage of exam marks earned.

Results display to two decimal places unless stated otherwise. Read our calculation methodology for scope and limitations.

Frequently asked questions

Is the 65th percentile the same as a 65% grade?

No. A grade describes your marks. A percentile describes where your score sits relative to a particular comparison group.

Why can the top score have a percentile below 100?

Midrank gives half-weight to tied scores, including your own. With a finite group this can place the highest score below 100.
